legend: A sequence of three positive integers [a,b,c]%%ZSMJ0%% is called a triangle if a+b>c%%ZSMJ1%% holds when reordered such that a≤b≤c%%ZSMJ2%%.
A sequence of positive integers is triangle-free if no subsequence of length 3%%ZSMJ3%% forms a triangle.

Given a sequence of positive integers L%%ZSMJ4%%, count how many non-empty subsequences of L%%ZSMJ5%% are triangle-free. As the answer may be very large, you are only required to find the value modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ6%%.
input: The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ7%% (1≤n≤7000%%ZSMJ8%%) — the size of the input sequence.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ9%% integers L1,L2,⋯,Ln%%ZSMJ10%% (1≤Li≤109%%ZSMJ11%%) — the elements of the sequence L%%ZSMJ12%%.
output: Output the number of non-empty triangle-free subsequences modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ13%% on one line.
